newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbekistan's grain harvest near end at 2.71 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan's grain harvest near end at 2.71 mln T.

text.p: Uzbekistan's grain harvest is 10-12 days from completion and stands at 2.71 million tonnes bunkered weight, up from 2.29 million tonnes at this time last year, a spokesman for the Ministry of Macroeconomics and Statistics said on Monday.

"Today in the republic, 2.71 million tonnes of grain have been gathered from 1.1 million hectares," the spokesman said. The harvest is falling far short of the former Soviet republic's four million tonne target. Uzbekistan's official grain output last year was 2.73 million tonnes.
According to the spokesman, a total of 1.49 million hectares were sown to grains. He said the average yield was 2.4 tonnes per hectare compared to year-ago levels of 2.2 tonnes.
Last month, an Agriculture Ministry official said higher yields and a faster rate of harvesting would see the largely desert nation of 23 million achieve its lofty four million-tonne target.

Uzbekistan, unable to achieve self-sufficiency in grain a second year running, is likely to be a large grain buyer this year. Trade sources say the Central Asian state imported about 1.6 million tonnes of wheat last year.

Poor irrigation, a lack of cash to upgrade the country's agriculture sector and stalled economic reforms have left Uzbekistan's farms stuck in a Soviet time-warp. Efforts to bale out hard-hit farmers with credits have quickened inflation and soured relations with the International Monetary Fund.
